enhanced.fullText:
The Trading with the Enemy Act of 1917 (TWEA), codified at 50 U.S.C. §§ 4301-4341, grants the President extraordinary authority to regulate or prohibit any transactions in foreign exchange, banking, and financial dealings during times of war or national emergency. Originally enacted during World War I, TWEA remains one of the most powerful economic warfare statutes in U.S. law, directly impacting higher education institutions engaged in international research, partnerships, and financial transactions.

Under 50 U.S.C. § 4305(b), the President may investigate, regulate, or prohibit any transactions involving foreign countries or nationals thereof, including educational exchanges, research collaborations, and technology transfers. The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), operating under Treasury Department authority pursuant to 31 CFR Parts 500-598, implements TWEA sanctions programs that universities must navigate carefully.

Higher education institutions face significant compliance obligations under TWEA, particularly regarding research activities involving sanctioned countries or entities listed on OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List. Universities conducting research with dual-use technologies must ensure compliance with both TWEA restrictions and Export Administration Regulations (EAR) under 15 CFR Parts 730-774. The intersection of these regulations creates complex compliance requirements for international research partnerships, student exchanges, and technology licensing agreements.

Key provisions affecting universities include prohibitions on transactions with blocked persons under 31 CFR § 501.201, mandatory blocking of assets under university control belonging to sanctioned entities, and restrictions on providing educational services that could benefit sanctioned countries' strategic capabilities. Universities must implement robust screening procedures for students, researchers, visiting scholars, and institutional partners against OFAC sanctions lists.

Violations carry severe penalties under 50 U.S.C. § 4315, including criminal fines up to $1 million for organizations and civil penalties up to $307,922 per violation as of 2023 adjustments under 31 CFR § 501.805. The Treasury Department has assessed significant penalties against universities for TWEA violations, including $100,000 against University of Massachusetts for unlicensed transactions with Iranian students.

Recent enforcement actions demonstrate OFAC's focus on higher education compliance. Universities must maintain comprehensive sanctions compliance programs including annual risk assessments, staff training, transaction monitoring systems, and detailed recordkeeping requirements under 31 CFR § 501.601. The complexity of modern university operations, including online education platforms serving global audiences, requires sophisticated compliance infrastructure to avoid inadvertent TWEA violations.
enhanced.summary: TWEA grants presidential authority to impose economic sanctions during wartime, requiring universities to screen international partnerships, block sanctioned entity assets, and maintain comprehensive compliance programs to avoid severe penalties.
enhanced.requirements:
## Sanctions Screening Requirements
- Screen all students, faculty, researchers, and institutional partners against OFAC SDN List and other sanctions lists
- Implement automated screening systems for ongoing monitoring of university community
- Conduct enhanced due diligence for high-risk countries and transactions
- Maintain screening documentation for audit purposes

## Asset Blocking Obligations
- Immediately freeze assets of any sanctioned persons identified on campus
- Report blocked assets to OFAC within required timeframes
- Prohibit any transactions involving blocked persons or entities
- Secure physical and electronic access to blocked assets

## Research and Technology Controls
- Review international research collaborations for sanctions implications
- Restrict technology transfers to sanctioned countries or entities
- Monitor dual-use research activities for compliance requirements
- Coordinate with export control officers on overlapping regulations

## Compliance Program Management
- Establish written sanctions compliance policies and procedures
- Conduct annual risk assessments of university sanctions exposure
- Provide regular training to relevant staff on TWEA obligations
- Maintain comprehensive records of sanctions compliance activities
enhanced.reportingRequirements: Universities must report blocked assets to OFAC within 10 business days via online reporting system. Annual compliance certifications required for certain license holders. Voluntary self-disclosure of potential violations recommended within 30 days of discovery.
